stemMd: A second exposure to the same antigen often produces a faster, stronger specific immune response. What principally explains this?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every antigen having the same structure

options.label: D
options.textMd: Permanent conversion of all red cells into antibodies

options.label: E
options.textMd: Absence of any need for lymphocytes

explanationMd: Some lymphocytes generated during the first response persist as memory cells. They can respond rapidly on re-exposure to the same antigen, explaining specificity and enhanced speed.

distractorRationale.d: Red cells do not become antibodies.
